actions.justification: Mandatory first step to fully characterize the patient's hemodynamic status. Patient has palpitations and dizziness - vital signs assessment is critical to determine stability and guide further management.

Mandatory diagnostic test to identify the underlying rhythm disturbance causing palpitations and dizziness. Critical for identifying atrial fibrillation, flutter, or other arrhythmias in a patient with mechanical heart valve.

Mandatory assessment for stroke risk stratification. Patient has hypertension and mechanical heart valve, both of which significantly elevate thromboembolic risk, making CHA2DS2-VASc scoring essential for anticoagulation decisions.

MANDATORY: Basic metabolic panel to evaluate electrolytes (K+, Mg2+), renal function, and glucose — all relevant to arrhythmia evaluation and medication management in a patient with palpitations and hypertension.
MANDATORY: Thyroid function testing is essential in the workup of new palpitations/arrhythmia, as hyperthyroidism is a common reversible cause of atrial fibrillation and other arrhythmias.

Continuous cardiac monitoring is indicated for a patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness to detect paroxysmal arrhythmias, assess rate control, and monitor hemodynamic stability — particularly important given the mechanical heart valve.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve, which requires careful anticoagulation management. With palpitations and dizziness, assessing anticoagulation need is critical — especially if AF is suspected, given the high thromboembolic risk associated with mechanical valves.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve and presenting arrhythmia symptoms. Cardiology consultation is warranted to guide management of potential atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmia in the context of a high-risk mechanical valve patient.
Electrophysiology consult is appropriate for a patient with palpitations, dizziness, and a mechanical heart valve to evaluate the arrhythmia etiology and help guide rhythm vs. rate control strategy.

Order a follow-up ECG to assess current rhythm and compare with baseline 12-lead already obtained, helping identify rate/rhythm changes over time in this patient with palpitations and mechanical heart valve.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve — a high-risk condition requiring anticoagulation. Heparin is indicated to bridge anticoagulation, especially if AF or other thromboembolic risk is identified on workup. Mechanical valve patients require continuous anticoagulation to prevent valve thrombosis and stroke.

Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for structural cardiac abnormalities, pulmonary congestion, or other thoracic pathology contributing to palpitations and dizziness in a patient with hypertension and mechanical heart valve.

Echocardiogram is essential in a patient with a mechanical heart valve presenting with palpitations to assess valve function, structural abnormalities, LV function, and rule out valve thrombosis or dysfunction.

CBC is needed to evaluate for anemia, infection, or thrombocytopenia which could contribute to palpitations and dizziness, and is relevant prior to anticoagulation decisions in a patient with mechanical heart valve.

Echocardiogram (via available action) is essential to assess mechanical valve function, evaluate for structural heart disease, and guide management of palpitations/dizziness in a patient with hypertension and mechanical heart valve.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve which mandates therapeutic anticoagulation. Pending INR/lab results, ensuring anticoagulation is maintained is critical to prevent thromboembolic complications in this high-risk patient.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve - INR monitoring is critical to ensure therapeutic anticoagulation and guide management. This is an urgent priority for any patient with a mechanical valve on anticoagulation.
Renal function assessment is important for drug dosing decisions (antiarrhythmics, anticoagulants) and to evaluate for any underlying cause of palpitations.
Full coagulation panel is indicated to assess bleeding/clotting risk, especially in a patient with a mechanical heart valve on anticoagulation therapy who may require procedural intervention.
Order troponin to rule out acute myocardial injury as a cause of the arrhythmia/palpitations in this patient with mechanical heart valve and hypertension.
Order NT-proBNP to assess for heart failure contribution to palpitations and dizziness, important in a patient with mechanical heart valve.
Order lactate to assess tissue perfusion status, as dizziness could indicate hemodynamic compromise.

Patient with palpitations, dizziness, hypertension, and mechanical heart valve likely has atrial fibrillation or another tachyarrhythmia. With HR currently 80 and stable vitals, rate control is appropriate initial management while awaiting diagnostic results. Beta blockers are relatively contraindicated with mechanical valves in some contexts, so general rate control approach is preferred pending ECG/lab results.

Digoxin can be considered for rate control in patients with mechanical heart valves who present with AF/palpitations, particularly when beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers may be less desirable. Provides rate control with positive hemodynamic profile in patients with valvular disease.
